natural_log_integration.description: The specific integration rule where the integral of 1/u du equals the natural logarithm of the absolute value of u (ln|u|).
common_misconceptions: Forgetting the absolute value brackets around u in ln|u|.
example_questions: Integrate tan(x) by using the substitution u = cos(x).

integration_by_substitution_trig.name: Trigonometric Integration via Substitution
integration_by_substitution_trig.description: Applying the substitution rule to trigonometric functions, often by substituting a trig function whose derivative is also present (e.g., substituting sine when cosine is present).
common_misconceptions: Choosing the wrong trigonometric function as 'u' (e.g., choosing cos for u when only sine is present).
example_questions: Integrate sin^6(x) * cos(x) dx using substitution.

matrix_basics.name: Matrix Basics
matrix_basics.description: Definition of a matrix as a rectangular arrangement of elements organized in horizontal rows and vertical columns.
common_misconceptions: Thinking only rectangular arrays are matrices, whereas square arrays are also matrices.
matrix_basics.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: What is the difference between a row and a column in a matrix?

matrix_indexing.name: Matrix Indexing and Order
matrix_indexing.description: Defining the size (order) of a matrix as M x N (rows by columns) and identifying specific elements using the notation a_ij, where i is the row number and j is the column number.
common_misconceptions: Swapping the order of rows and columns (e.g., calling a 3x2 matrix a 2x3 matrix).
matrix_indexing.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: In a 3x5 matrix, what are the indices of the element in the 2nd row and 4th column?

matrix_multiplication.name: Matrix Multiplication
matrix_multiplication.description: The process of computing the product of two matrices, requiring that the number of columns in the first matrix equals the number of rows in the second.
common_misconceptions: Assuming matrix multiplication is commutative (AB = BA).
matrix_multiplication.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: If matrix A is 3x4 and matrix B is 4x2, what is the order of the resulting matrix AB?

matrix_transpose.name: Matrix Transpose
matrix_transpose.description: An operation that flips a matrix over its diagonal, interchanging its row and column indices (A_ij becomes A_ji).
common_misconceptions: Confusing transpose with the inverse of a matrix.
Thinking transpose changes the values of the elements
matrix_transpose.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Given a 2x3 matrix, what will be the order of its transpose?
Find the transpose of a 2x3 matrix.

symmetric_matrix.name: Symmetric Matrix
symmetric_matrix.description: A square matrix that is equal to its own transpose (A = A^T), meaning elements are mirrored across the principal diagonal.
common_misconceptions: Thinking any matrix with equal values in the first and last row is symmetric.
Thinking symmetry only applies to the visual layout and not the mathematical property a_ij = a_ji
symmetric_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Verify if a matrix where a_ij = a_ji for all i, j is symmetric.
Determine if a given 3x3 matrix is symmetric.

skew_symmetric_matrix.name: Skew-Symmetric Matrix
skew_symmetric_matrix.description: A square matrix where A^T = -A, meaning elements across the diagonal have opposite signs, and all principal diagonal elements must be zero.
common_misconceptions: Forgetting that the principal diagonal elements must be zero for a matrix to be skew-symmetric.
Forgetting that diagonal elements must be zero in a skew-symmetric matrix
skew_symmetric_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Why must the diagonal elements of a skew-symmetric matrix always be zero?
Why must the diagonal elements of a skew-symmetric matrix be zero?
global_doubts: If I change a 0 on the diagonal to a 1, does the matrix just stop being skew-symmetric, or does it become something else?
If I change a 0 on the diagonal to a 1, does the matrix just stop being skew-symmetric, or does it become something else?

diagonal_matrix.name: Diagonal Matrix
diagonal_matrix.description: A square matrix where all elements outside the principal diagonal are zero.
common_misconceptions: Thinking the diagonal elements themselves must be non-zero.
Believing that the diagonal elements themselves must be non-zero
diagonal_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Is a null matrix also a diagonal matrix?
Is a matrix with all zeros a diagonal matrix?

identity_matrix.name: Identity Matrix
identity_matrix.description: A special diagonal matrix where all principal diagonal elements are 1 and all other elements are 0.
common_misconceptions: Confusing the identity matrix with a matrix of all ones.
Confusing the identity matrix with a matrix of all ones
identity_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: What happens when any square matrix A is multiplied by the identity matrix I?
What is the 2x2 identity matrix?

orthogonal_matrix.name: Orthogonal Matrix
orthogonal_matrix.description: A square matrix A such that A multiplied by its transpose results in the identity matrix (A * A^T = I).
common_misconceptions: Thinking every matrix with a determinant of 1 is orthogonal.
orthogonal_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Prove that the determinant of an orthogonal matrix is either 1 or -1.

idempotent_matrix.name: Idempotent Matrix
idempotent_matrix.description: A square matrix that, when multiplied by itself, yields the original matrix (A^2 = A).
common_misconceptions: Thinking A^2 = A implies A must be the identity matrix.
idempotent_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: If a matrix is idempotent, what are the possible values for its determinant?

involutory_matrix.name: Involutory Matrix
involutory_matrix.description: A square matrix that is its own inverse, meaning A squared equals the identity matrix (A^2 = I).
common_misconceptions: Confusing involutory matrices (A^2 = I) with idempotent matrices (A^2 = A).
involutory_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: If A is involutory, what is A inverse?

nilpotent_matrix.name: Nilpotent Matrix
nilpotent_matrix.description: A non-zero square matrix A such that some positive integer power n results in the zero matrix (A^n = 0). The smallest such n is called the index of nilpotency.
common_misconceptions: Thinking the matrix must be the zero matrix to satisfy A^n = 0.
nilpotent_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Find the index of nilpotency for a matrix if A^3 = 0 but A^2 != 0.

matrix_minor_cofactor.name: Matrix Minors and Cofactors
matrix_minor_cofactor.description: A minor is the determinant of a submatrix formed by deleting a specific row and column. A cofactor is a minor multiplied by (-1)^(i+j).
common_misconceptions: Forgetting to apply the alternating sign (-1)^(i+j) when calculating cofactors.
matrix_minor_cofactor.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Calculate the cofactor of the element a_12 in a 3x3 matrix.

matrix_determinant.name: Matrix Determinant
matrix_determinant.description: A scalar value derived from a square matrix, computed as the sum of elements of any row or column multiplied by their corresponding cofactors.
common_misconceptions: Trying to calculate the determinant of a non-square matrix.
matrix_determinant.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Compute the determinant of a 3x3 matrix using expansion along the second column.

determinant_properties.name: Properties of Determinants
determinant_properties.description: Rules for determinants, such as |A^T| = |A|, |kA| = k^n|A|, and the fact that swapping two rows changes the sign of the determinant.
common_misconceptions: Thinking |kA| = k|A| instead of k to the power of n times |A|.
determinant_properties.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: If |A| = 5 and A is a 3x3 matrix, what is |2A|?

adjoint_matrix.name: Adjoint Matrix
adjoint_matrix.description: The transpose of the cofactor matrix of a square matrix A.
common_misconceptions: Confusing the adjoint matrix with the inverse matrix.
adjoint_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: What is the relationship between A, adj(A), and det(A)?

matrix_inverse.name: Matrix Inverse
matrix_inverse.description: A square matrix A inverse such that A * A inverse = I. It is computed as (1/det(A)) * adj(A).
common_misconceptions: Assuming every square matrix has an inverse.
Thinking that the inverse is simply the reciprocal of each element
matrix_inverse.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Find the inverse of a 2x2 matrix using the adjoint method.
Find the inverse of a 2x2 matrix.

matrix_singularity.name: Matrix Singularity
matrix_singularity.description: A square matrix is called singular if its determinant is zero, meaning it does not have an inverse.
common_misconceptions: Thinking a matrix with a zero element on the diagonal is automatically singular.
matrix_singularity.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: How can you determine if a matrix is singular without finding its inverse?

row_echelon_form.name: Row Echelon Form (REF)
row_echelon_form.description: A matrix form where all zero rows are at the bottom and the number of leading zeros in a row is strictly greater than the number of leading zeros in the row above it.
common_misconceptions: Confusing Row Echelon Form with Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF).
row_echelon_form.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Convert a given 3x4 matrix into Row Echelon Form using elementary row operations.

matrix_rank.name: Matrix Rank
matrix_rank.description: The dimension of the vector space generated by its rows or columns, practically found as the number of non-zero rows in its Row Echelon Form.
common_misconceptions: Thinking the rank is just the number of non-zero elements in the matrix.
matrix_rank.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: What is the maximum possible rank of a 3x5 matrix?

augmented_matrix.name: Augmented Matrix
augmented_matrix.description: A matrix formed by appending the constant vector B as an additional column to the coefficient matrix A in a system of linear equations.
common_misconceptions: Incorrectly adding the constant vector as a row instead of a column.
augmented_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Write the augmented matrix for a system of three equations with three unknowns.

linear_system_consistency.name: Consistency of Linear Systems
linear_system_consistency.description: The analysis of whether a system AX=B has solutions. It is consistent if rank(A) = rank(A|B). It has a unique solution if this rank equals the number of unknowns, and infinite solutions otherwise.
common_misconceptions: Thinking a system with rank(A) < n always has no solution.
linear_system_consistency.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Given rank(A) = 2 and rank(A|B) = 3, does the system have a solution?

homogeneous_linear_systems.name: Homogeneous Linear Systems
homogeneous_linear_systems.description: A system of equations AX=0. These systems are always consistent and always possess the trivial solution (X=0). Non-trivial solutions exist only if det(A) = 0.
common_misconceptions: Thinking a homogeneous system can be inconsistent (have no solution).
homogeneous_linear_systems.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Under what condition does a homogeneous system have non-trivial solutions?

linear_combination.name: Linear Combination
linear_combination.description: An expression formed by multiplying vectors by scalars and adding the results (e.g., k1V1 + k2V2 + ... + knVn).
common_misconceptions: Thinking linear combinations only involve adding vectors without scalar multiplication.
Assuming coefficients must be integers
linear_combination.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Express the vector [3, 4] as a linear combination of [1, 0] and [0, 1].
Express vector b as a linear combination of vectors v1 and v2.

linear_independence.name: Linear Independence
linear_independence.description: A set of vectors is linearly independent if the only scalars that satisfy the linear combination k1V1 + ... + knVn = 0 are k1 = k2 = ... = kn = 0.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that if vectors are not parallel, they must be linearly independent in 3D space.
Assuming vectors are independent just because they aren't parallel (true for 2, not necessarily for 3+)
linear_independence.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Determine if the set of vectors {[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]} is linearly independent.
Test whether a set of three vectors in R3 is linearly independent.

matrix_definition.name: Matrix Definition
matrix_definition.description: A rectangular array of elements organized into horizontal rows and vertical columns, denoted by capital letters.
common_misconceptions: Confusing rows with columns when identifying elements
matrix_definition.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics 01 | Linear Algebra (Part 01) | GATE 2025 series | All Branch
example_questions: What is a matrix in linear algebra?

matrix_order.name: Matrix Order (Size)
matrix_order.description: The dimensions of a matrix expressed as m by n (m x n), where m is the number of rows and n is the number of columns.
common_misconceptions: Listing columns before rows (n x m instead of m x n)
matrix_order.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics 01 | Linear Algebra (Part 01) | GATE 2025 series | All Branch
example_questions: If a matrix has 3 rows and 4 columns, what is its order?

square_matrix.name: Square Matrix
square_matrix.description: A matrix where the number of rows equals the number of columns (m = n).
common_misconceptions: Thinking all matrices must be square to have a determinant
square_matrix.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics 01 | Linear Algebra (Part 01) | GATE 2025 series | All Branch
example_questions: Is a 3x2 matrix a square matrix?

principal_diagonal.name: Principal Diagonal
principal_diagonal.description: The collection of elements a_ii in a square matrix where the row index equals the column index.
common_misconceptions: Confusing the principal diagonal with the anti-diagonal
principal_diagonal.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics 01 | Linear Algebra (Part 01) | GATE 2025 series | All Branch
example_questions: Identify the principal diagonal elements of a 3x3 matrix.

matrix_trace.name: Matrix Trace
matrix_trace.description: The sum of all elements on the principal diagonal of a square matrix.
common_misconceptions: Attempting to calculate the trace of a non-square matrix
matrix_trace.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics 01 | Linear Algebra (Part 01) | GATE 2025 series | All Branch
example_questions: Calculate the trace of a matrix with diagonal elements 2, -1, and 5.

row_picture.name: Row Picture of Linear Equations
row_picture.description: Viewing a system of linear equations as the intersection of geometric objects (lines in 2D, planes in 3D) where each equation represents one object.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that three planes always meet at a single point
example_questions: Describe the row picture for a 2x2 system of equations.

column_picture.name: Column Picture of Linear Equations
column_picture.description: Viewing a system Ax = b as finding the right linear combination of the columns of A that produces vector b.
common_misconceptions: Confusing the column picture with the row picture (mixing up intersections and combinations)
example_questions: How does the column picture differ from the row picture in solving Ax = b?

matrix_vector_multiplication.name: Matrix-Vector Multiplication
matrix_vector_multiplication.description: The process of multiplying a matrix A by a vector x, which can be interpreted as a linear combination of the columns of A weighted by the entries of x.
common_misconceptions: Multiplying element-by-element instead of using the dot product/combination method
example_questions: Multiply a 2x2 matrix by a 2x1 vector using the column interpretation.

span.name: Span
span.description: The set of all possible linear combinations of a given set of vectors, representing the portion of space they can reach.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that the span of two vectors is always a 2D plane (they could be collinear)
span.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: What is the span of two non-parallel vectors in R2?

gaussian_elimination.name: Gaussian Elimination
gaussian_elimination.description: A systematic process of using elementary row operations (swapping, scaling, adding) to transform a matrix into a simpler form to solve linear systems.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that row operations change the solution set of the system
gaussian_elimination.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: Use Gaussian elimination to solve a 3x3 system of equations.

reduced_row_echelon_form.name: Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF)
reduced_row_echelon_form.description: The simplest version of a matrix after Gaussian elimination, where each leading entry is 1 and is the only non-zero entry in its column.
common_misconceptions: Stopping at row echelon form and thinking it is RREF
reduced_row_echelon_form.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: Convert a given matrix into its RREF.

pivot_position.name: Pivot Position
pivot_position.description: The first non-zero entry in a row of a matrix in row echelon form, used to determine the number of solutions and the rank.
common_misconceptions: Assuming pivots must be 1 in the initial matrix
pivot_position.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: How many pivot positions are in the RREF of a given matrix?

determinant.name: Determinant
determinant.description: A scalar value derived from a square matrix that describes whether the matrix is invertible and how the associated transformation changes volume/orientation.
common_misconceptions: Believing that a zero determinant means the matrix is 'empty' rather than singular
determinant.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: Calculate the determinant of a 3x3 matrix.

basis.name: Basis
basis.description: The smallest possible set of linearly independent vectors that span a given vector space.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that there is only one unique basis for a space
basis.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: Find a basis for the span of three given vectors.

dimension.name: Dimension
dimension.description: The number of vectors present in any basis of a vector space.
common_misconceptions: Confusing the dimension of a subspace with the number of components in its vectors
dimension.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: What is the dimension of R3?

linear_transformation.name: Linear Transformation
linear_transformation.description: A mapping between vectors that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication, often represented by matrix multiplication.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that all functions mapping vectors to vectors are linear
linear_transformation.lecture_source: ALL of linear algebra in 7 minutes.
example_questions: How does a matrix transform the basis vectors of R2?

eigenvalue.name: Eigenvalue
eigenvalue.description: A scalar lambda such that Ax = lambda*x for some non-zero vector x. It represents the scaling factor of the eigenvector during transformation.
common_misconceptions: Assuming eigenvalues must be real numbers (they can be complex)
eigenvalue.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Find the eigenvalues of a 2x2 matrix.

eigenvector.name: Eigenvector
eigenvector.description: A non-zero vector x that changes only in magnitude (not direction) when multiplied by a matrix A: Ax = lambda*x.
common_misconceptions: Including the zero vector as an eigenvector
eigenvector.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Find the eigenvector corresponding to a specific eigenvalue.

characteristic_equation.name: Characteristic Equation
characteristic_equation.description: The equation det(A - lambda*I) = 0, whose roots are the eigenvalues of matrix A.
common_misconceptions: Forgetting to subtract lambda from the diagonal elements before calculating the determinant
characteristic_equation.lecture_source: Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices) | GATE 2023 | For All Branches
example_questions: Derive the characteristic equation for a given 2x2 matrix.
